answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit confirms fabricated work. The audit is tied to task evidence and sampled across operators, so creating many identities does not multiply honest-looking results for free. A sybil attacker must buy and immobilize more stake, risk losing it on each caught lie, and still pay for real compute; marble, violet, and glacier can label three audited jobs without changing that cost.
